sources.title: Library of Congress, North Korea: A Country Study (2008)
sources.note: Original 384-page PDF downloaded; fifth edition 2008, research completed October 2007. Printed xvi, xxxii, 45 to 47 and 142 to 145 checked. Chronology contains errors about armistice signatories and the first nuclear-test date; those claims use independent primary sources instead.

sources.title: US National Archives, Korean Armistice Agreement, 27 July 1953
sources.note: Original archive page and agreement transcript checked. Preamble identifies military parties; Article I requires withdrawal two kilometres each side. The armistice stopped hostilities but was not a peace treaty.

sources.title: Congressional Research Service, North Korea: U.S. Relations, Nuclear Diplomacy, and Internal Situation, 27 July 2018
sources.note: Original PDF checked, printed 1 and 14/PDF 18. Dated 2018, not a current leadership assessment. All R41259 versions grouped as one work for budgets.

sources.title: United Nations General Assembly resolution 46/1, 17 September 1991
sources.note: Original UN catalogue identifies admission of both Korean states, adopted without a vote on 17 September 1991. Catalogue publication date is not the admission date.

sources.title: CTBTO, Detecting nuclear tests
sources.note: Original institutional account checked: six declared DPRK tests, 2006 to 2017. For 2006, seismic stations and xenon-133 detected at Yellowknife. No weapon yield or stockpile estimate inferred.

sources.title: UN Security Council, 1718 Sanctions Committee
sources.note: Original measures table checked. Arms embargo and asset freeze; historical sanctions framework, not operational legal advice.

sources.title: UN Security Council, Implementation Assistance Notice 7, updated 2 June 2023
sources.note: Original six-page PDF directly checked, pp. 1 to 2: humanitarian exceptions and case-by-case exemptions. Group with 1718 institutional material conservatively.

sources.title: UN Commission of Inquiry on human rights in the DPRK, A/HRC/25/63, 7 February 2014
sources.note: Original 36-page report directly checked: paragraphs 9 to 16 access and methods; 29 information restrictions; 32 to 33 songbun; 80 findings. Commission findings are attributed, not presented as a criminal court judgment.

sources.title: Elizabeth Salmón, UN Special Rapporteur statement, 19 March 2025
sources.note: Original six-page statement checked: p. 2 prolonged isolation and lack of UN humanitarian presence; pp. 4 to 6 food, health, education and access limits. Statistical dates retained.

sources.title: World Food Programme, Democratic People’s Republic of Korea country account
sources.note: Full indexed original country account checked: limited land and agricultural inputs, food access, relatives, kitchen gardens and markets. Avoid ambiguous headline counts and claims that every planned operation is currently delivered.

sources.title: UNESCO, Pyongyang Raengmyon custom, inscribed 2022
sources.note: Full indexed original entry and inscription decision checked; direct entry hits JavaScript challenge. Brass bowl, buckwheat, garnishes, long-life associations and intergenerational transmission. Do not infer unchanged ancient origins or universal food availability.

sources.title: UNESCO, Arirang folk song in the DPRK, inscribed 2014
sources.note: Full indexed original entry checked, including family, community and school transmission. Downloaded nomination link returned HTML challenge, not a verified PDF. No lyrics reproduced.

sources.title: Republic of Korea official transcript, Panmunjom Declaration, 27 April 2018
sources.note: Official Korean transcript directly checked, title and closing date/signatories. Short sample is part of the title of a joint inter-Korean document, not a DPRK-only publication. Romanization editorial Revised Romanization; English title also verified against Ministry of Unification archive record 675. Group all declaration mirrors as one work.

sources.title: UNICEF DPRK, Water, sanitation and hygiene
sources.note: Original page directly checked. The 2017 MICS figure of 93% applies to people in households using improved on-site sanitation and unsafe or partial treatment/disposal, not to all residents lacking toilets. Narrative avoids an easy-to-misread percentage.

sources.title: UNICEF, Delivering clean drinking water to children in DPR Korea, 6 November 2019
sources.note: Full indexed original report checked: gravity-fed Myonggan system, 16,000 people, eight nurseries/kindergartens, six schools and two health facilities. Local report, not nationwide access statistic.

sources.title: WHO, Nationwide catch-up immunization campaign in DPR Korea, 26 April 2023
sources.note: Full indexed original account checked: March campaign for missed doses in 2021 to 2022, local clinics/nurseries, waiting, registration, vaccination and observation arrangements.

sources.title: UNICEF, Nearly one million children and pregnant women to receive life-saving vaccines, 3 September 2024
sources.note: Original press release directly checked: campaign launched with target over 800,000 children and 120,000 pregnant women; cold boxes, refrigerators/freezers and temperature loggers. Targets are not verified completion totals.

sources.title: UN DPPA, This Week in DPPA, 25 April to 1 May 2026
sources.note: Indexed original account checked: 30 April 2026 Security Council briefing by Rosemary DiCarlo on DPRK nuclear and missile programmes. Direct page fetch failed. Dated continuity evidence, not a live September 2026 assessment.

scopeNotes: New text needs independent review; earlier hashes do not certify it.
Map endpoints are not historical founding or extinction dates.
Agent researched a disjoint batch; integration and structural checks are not independent historical certification.
Imported border coordinates remain unchanged. Historical events and map coverage are distinguished in prose; see batchIdentityNotes for conflicts.

proposedOverrides.summary: The modern North Korean state, from founding and war through centralized rule, household adaptation, cultural practices and uneven access to basic services.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: Exact modern DPRK only. Index begins 1960 although founding is 1948; geometry intervals 1960 to 1994, 1994 to 2000, 2000 to 2010 and 2010 to 2020. All four include Pyongyang, Kaesong and Hamhung tests but exclude Chongjin and include Dandong in China; public overview explicitly warns about these coarse-border errors. Do not merge Korea (USA), South Korea or earlier Korean polities. Open-ended state continuity, no invented fall or successor. Political and humanitarian findings retain their report dates and access limits.
